title: Maximum-modulus points of entire functions (Erdős Problem 1117), in Lean 4
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of both maximum-modulus counting questions of Hayman–Lingham Problem 2.16 (Erdős Problem 1117). For an entire function f and a radius r, let ν(f, r) be the number of points on the circle |z| = r where |f| attains its maximum on that circle. The registered theorem proves two things: some non-monomial entire function has ν(f, r) unbounded along radii tending to infinity; and for every non-monomial entire function there is one finite bound B with ν(f, r) ≤ B along a cofinal set of radii, so the counts never tend to infinity. The first part follows Pardo-Simón and Sixsmith's finite-order construction and proves the approximation step of Rempe-Gillen that it uses; the second follows Li's cofinal-bound argument. The theorem depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
